# KIT-REFERENCE (generated by `node assets/kit/kit-reference.mjs`; never edit by hand)

One line per export: `name(signature)`, what it is; the most used ones with their whole doc. Lists show their ids. When this page does not explain something, Read or Grep the kit source (assets/kit).

## core.js
_The Explainers world kit, core (hx-4, visual system 4.0; from Explainer 2.0): the style-independent math every shot stands on._

- `VERSION` = "hx-4"
- `FRAME` = { w, h, safe }
- `TOKENS` = { paper, paper-lit, paper-shade, paper-dark, paper-sweep, canvas, ink, ink-lit, ink-shade, ink-dark, text-secondary, text-tertiary, orange, orange-lit, orange-shade, orange-dark, orange-text, green, green-lit, green-shade, green-dark, yellow, yellow-lit, yellow-shade, yellow-dark, blue, blue-lit, blue-shade, blue-dark, teal, teal-lit, teal-shade, teal-dark, lilac, lilac-lit, lilac-shade, lilac-dark, red, red-lit, red-shade, red-dark, night, stage-top, stage-bottom, stage-orange, stage-red, sun-to… } (54 keys)
- `PALETTE` = [paper, ink, orange, green, yellow, blue, teal, lilac, red] — The palette colors that have a 4-step ramp, by name.
- `ramp(name)` — A palette color's ramp: { lit, base, shade, dark }.
- `mixHex(a, b, t)` — Two hex colors mixed in linear light (t = share of b), as hex: the tints and falloffs a soft volume needs between the steps of one ramp.
- `TONE_ALIASES` = { white } — Names a tone may also go by: `white` is the canvas (the outfits palette says white).
- `toneNames()` — Every color name a tone may use: the ramp names, the palette tokens and the aliases.
- `resolveTone(v)` — The one tone resolver (4.1): what every lens/draw solid and every set piece is painted from.
- `toneHex(v)` — A tone as one hex: a ramp name gives its base.
- `clamp(v, lo, hi)`
- `tok(name)`
- `mix(a, b, t)` — A mix of exactly two palette tokens (V-T1).
- `alpha(a, opacity)` — A palette token at an opacity, 0..1.
- `GROUNDS` = { paper, stage, white } — The grounds (hx-4): `paper` the warm studio sweep (default), `stage` the Helios premium lit stage (the one dark ground), `white` the close only.
- `GROUND_ALIASES` = { night, forest } — Grounds 4.0 retired, drawn as the stage so old projects still render (a storyboard naming them is a lint error).
- `groundOf(name = 'paper')` — A ground by name, aliases resolved: { name, fill, dark }.
- `LIGHT` = { key, ambient, bounce } — key: the screen direction the key light comes FROM (toward the top right); ambient: the share of light a face turned away still gets; bounce: the war…
- `CRITTER_CM` = 72 — A critter's real height in cm: the ruler every world entity is sized against.
- `CRITTER_PX` = 142 — A critter's drawn height at s = 1 in px, feet (y 0) to the top of its body (y −142, cast.js).
- `PX_PER_CM` = 1.9722222222222223 — Screen px per cm at scale 1.
- `CHEAT` = { readCm, max } — Scale is believable, not true (4.2, house style): things stay plausible next to each other, and the props the action depends on are cheated bigger so…
- `propScale(scale, sizeCm)`
    The factor a prop is drawn at: `scale` 'cheat' (CHEAT, from its real size `sizeCm`, a number or
    [w, d, h] in cm), a positive number (that factor), or nothing (1, its real size). Anything else
    throws, saying what it takes.
    @param {'cheat' | number | undefined | null} scale
    @param {number | number[]} [sizeCm]
- `POLARITY` = { linear, slam, snap, ramp-up, glide, spring, reverse, drift, ramp } (9 keys)
- `polarity(name)`
- `makeWarp(ramps, duration)`
- `resolveRamps(ramps, duration)` — Ramps given by the CONTENT moment they slow (`around`), resolved to wall time (V-9).
- `cam(c)`
- `lerpCam(a, b, f)`
- `camAt(start, legs, t)` — Camera at content time t, from a start camera and non-overlapping legs.
- `cameraTransform(c, cx = FRAME.w / 2, cy = FRAME.h / 2)` — The SVG transform of the world under camera c, pivoting on (cx, cy).
- `CAMERA_LIMITS` = { maxZoomRatio, maxRoll, maxTilt }
- `validateLegs(legs, duration, start)`
- `ledgerValue(start, changes, t)`
- `rng(seed)`
- `FPS_CAST` = 15 — The old pose rate; mark.js still rounds its landing cue to it.
- `FPS_BOIL` = 10 — The old wobble rate (no wobble is drawn any more).
- `onTwos(t)` — Smooth motion: returns t unchanged (it used to hold each pose for two frames).
- `boilSeed(_t = 0)` — No boil in hx-4: the seed never changes (kept for old callers, which pass t).
- `ISO_COS` = 0.8660254037844387
- `ISO_SIN` = 0.5
- `iso(ox, oy, s = 1)` — World (x right-back, y left-back, z up) → screen, with world origin at (ox, oy), scale s.
- `isoPlane(P, s, x, y, z = 0)` — The SVG transform that lays flat 2D drawing (u along world x, v along world y) on the plane z, with its origin at world (x, y).

## light.js
_The Explainers world kit, light (hx-4, approved still 14 "light as motion"): light is animated, not_

- `hashId(s)` — A short stable name for a piece of content (ids are content-addressed, so equal defs share one).
- `blurDef(sd, { box = [-400, -400, 1880, 2720], name = 'blur' } = {})` — A Gaussian blur filter of `sd` px: `{ defs, url }`.

```
Cut grammar (Explainers 4.1; 4.2) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A camera shot: { at, kind, camera: { pos, target, fov }, subject: 'id', cast: ['id', …],
place?: 'id' (a world.js SETS place; 'main' when absent),
move?: { kind: 'push' | 'pull' | 'pan' | 'follow' | 'track', by? (cm), deg?, at?, dur?, e? },
focus?: { reason: 'insert' | 'reveal' | 'rack', on: 'id', to?: 'id', at?, dur? },
subjectAt?: [x, y, z] (the subject's world point; the camera's target when absent) }.
The camera is the only reframing: no `on`, `zoom` or `push` crop on top of it.
```

- `animalFrom(draw, x, y, { kind = 'animal', cm, units, view = 'side', s = 1, flip = false, t = 0 } = {})`
    Any animal drawn with ANIMAL_PARTS: `draw(t)` returns its volumes in units, feet at (0, 0); `cm` is its real height (a small one is cheated up by core CHEAT) and `units` the drawing's height. Feet at (x, y).
- `animal(kind, x, y, { view = 'side', s = 1, flip = false, t = 0, action = false } = {})`
    A real animal from the kit (ANIMALS: puppy, songbird, horse), feet at (x, y). `s` is the critter scale (s 1 = a 142 px critter); `view` 'side' (primary) or 'front'; `flip` mirrors it (the light stays top right); `action` plays its one natural action over `t`.

## objects.js
_The Explainers world kit, objects and motion (4.2, PLAN turns 11–15): the real things a mechanism_

- `READ_MIN` = 34 — The smallest text read in a mechanism frame (= explain.js READ_MIN; explain.js imports this module for the identity map, so the value is restated her…
- `OBJECTS` = { laptop, phone, tablet, screen, server, rack, chip, database, router, cloud, document, folder, envelope, box, key, lock, card, speaker } (18 keys) — The object library: id → { states, hinge (true when it opens and closes), mass, accent (the part orange marks), label ('plate' | 'screen') }.
- `OBJECT_IDS` = [laptop, phone, tablet, screen, server, rack, chip, database, router, cloud, document, folder, envelope, box, key, lock, card, speaker]
- `PIN_NAMES` = [base, center, top, front, hinge] — The puppet pins every object has (`hinge` only on the objects that open).
- `COURIER_KINDS` = [request, packet, file, message] — The travelling kinds a courier draws besides any OBJECTS id.
- `REACTIONS` = [surprised, proud, worried, no, yes] — The motion reactions (objects act through motion alone).
- `VERBS` = [hopTo, slideTo, lookAt, react, nod, shake, openHinge, closeHinge, settle, breathe, setState, setAccent]
- `FACE_KEYS` = [face, eyes, eye, mouth, mood, brows, brow, expression, look, lid, lids, pupil, pupils, smile, blink, cheeks, emotion, gaze] — Options that would give an object a face: refused everywhere (house style).
- `OBJECT_PORTS` = { laptop, phone, tablet, screen, server, rack, router, speaker, database, chip } (10 keys) — Each device's port names (connect.js plugs cables into them).
- `OBJECT_CM` = { laptop, phone, tablet, screen, server, rack, chip, database, router, cloud, document, folder, envelope, box, key, lock, card, speaker } (18 keys)
- `toneFamily(tone)` — A body tone as the colour name an identity check compares: 'blue' for 'blue' or 'blue-shade', `mix(a,b)` for a mix, 'own' for the object's own tone.
- `object(objId, at, opts = {})`
    A real-world thing, standing with its base centre at screen `at` ([x, y]): for mechanism frames,
    blend frames and flat overlays (the isometric table).
      size     scale (1 ≈ 240–340 px wide; cheat what the action depends on bigger)
      accent   true / 0..1: its accent part in orange (what to look at now); default off
      label    a short label on the thing (1–3 words), ≥ READ_MIN
      state    one of OBJECTS[id].states (default the first)
      tone     its body colour: a palette tone, never orange (default per object)
      facing   'left' (front to the lower left, default) or 'right'
      floor    the screen y of the surface it stands on (default at[1]): objectProblems flags it below
      key      its identity on the timeline (default `${id}@x,y`)
      labelSize  the label's size (default clamp(40 × size, 34, 52))
      concept  the identity-map concept it stands for (explain.js identity(); reg.object() sets it)
    Returns a handle { id, key, at, size, pins (rest), box (rest), pin(name), draw(t, segments),
    pose(t, segments), pinsAt(t, segments) } that also stringifies to its SVG at rest.
- `worldObject(objId, at, opts = {})`
    The same thing standing in a perspective world (lens.js, cm, z up) at `at` ([x, y] or [x, y, z],
    its base centre on the floor or on a surface at height z): for world frames, an object hero in a
    room. Drawn with lensObject(P, obj, { t, segments, rig }) as one of render()'s items: placed and
    scaled by depth, turned three-quarters to the lens like a critter (`facing` picks which side shows),
    lit by the shot's rig (night included) with its contact shadow and the shadows its lights cast.
    `size` is its scale against its true size (OBJECT_CM; 1 = true, 'cheat' = cheated bigger so it
    reads, or a number). Other options as object() (no `floor`: the world has its own). The verbs move
    it through world positions (cm): hopTo(obj, [x, y]), slideTo, lookAt(obj, [x, y, z]), …
- `lensObject(P, obj, o = {})`
    A world object at t through the lens P, as a render() item: { id, at, bounds, svg, pins, box, dist }.
    `id` is its key (a shot's cast names it), `at` its mid-height (cm), `bounds` its world box for the
    paint order, `pins` its screen pins at t (hang a label, a courier or a camera target on them), `box`
    its screen box. Options: t (frame time), segments (its moves), rig (the shot's lens.js rig; its
    light, colour and shadows; a plain day studio when absent).

- `portsAt(obj, t, segments = [])` — A screen object's ports at t: { name: { screen, sdir } }, for connect.js screenCable.
- `pinsAt(obj, t, segments = [])`

- `slideTo(obj, to, o = {})` — slideTo(obj, to, { at, dur }): pushed along the floor to `to`: a small counter-lean first, the top lags as it accelerates and runs on as it brakes (f…
- `lookAt(obj, target, o = {})` — lookAt(obj, target, { at, dur, amount }): the object tilts toward `target` (a point, an object or a pin; null turns it back upright) and holds there:…
- `react(obj, kind, o = {})` — react(obj, kind, { at, dur }): a motion reaction, never a face.
- `nod(obj, o = {})` — nod(obj, { at, times, dur }): the top tips toward the front and back, smaller each time, settling.
- `shake(obj, o = {})` — shake(obj, { at, times, dur }): side to side about its base, smaller each swing, then settles.

- `markOk(box)` — True when the box, grown by its clear space on every side, sits inside the safe area (V-T3), and its width is within V-19's 40 to 55% of the frame.
- `markContact(at, dur = 1.0)` — Shot time of the frame where the mark touches the table, for a landing that starts at `at`: the first on-twos frame at or after contact.
- `markLanding(t, at, { cx, cy, width = DEFAULT_WIDTH, dark = false, dur = 1.0 })` — The mark landing at shot time `at`, centered at rest on (cx, cy), `width` px wide, over `dur` seconds. Returns '' before it starts.
